messages.subject: Questions about Delta/Hurdle Gamma model
parts:
Hi folks

I’m currently self-studying spatial modeling but struggling to find the right approach.

My dependent variable is a right-skewed continuous variable with a high proportion of zeros (over 50%, n = 3,045 counties). The geometry data comes from the US Census data from tidycensus package, and it is stored as an sfc or sf object (seemingly polygons).

Given the high proportion of zeros, I believe a hurdle model is appropriate. While I plan to examine both spatial and temporal effects in the future, I am currently focusing only on the spatial effects for a single year. My goal is to determine whether there is a diffusion effect in the IV, DV, or error term.

I attempted to use sdmTMB to fit a hurdle Gamma model following this page (https://pbs-assess.github.io/sdmTMB/articles/delta-models.html) but encountered several challenges:

1. sdmTMB seems to be useful for point data. Would it be appropriate to extract coordinates from the polygons and convert them into point data for estimation?

2. I tried using sanity() to assess model fit, but it resulted in an error. Could this indicate that my data is problematic?

3. When I apply a log(x+1) transformation to the DV, the nonzero values become approximately normally distributed. Should I log-transform the DV before running a Gamma hurdle model?


df.g <- st_read("all23.g.gpkg")
df.g <- df.g |> na.omit() 
centroids <- st_centroid(df.g)

centroid_coords <- st_coordinates(centroids)
pcod <- data.frame(X = centroid_coords[, 1], 
                   Y = centroid_coords[, 2]) 

mesh <- make_mesh(pcod, c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 15)

df.drop <- df.g %>% 
  st_drop_geometry()

fit_dg <- sdmTMB(solpckwk ~ edu + hsp + blk + incmk,
                 data = df.drop,
                 mesh = mesh,
                 family = delta_gamma(),
                 spatial = list("on", "on"))

print(fit_dg)

Spatial model fit by ML ['sdmTMB'] Formula: solpckwk ~ edu + hsp + blk + incmk Mesh: pcod_mesh (isotropic covariance) Data: df.drop Family: delta_gamma(link1 = 'logit', link2 = 'log') Delta/hurdle model 1: ----------------------------------- Family: binomial(link = 'logit') coef.est coef.se (Intercept) -2.22 0.55 edu 0.02 0.01 hsp 0.04 0.01 blk 0.04 0.00 incmk 0.02 0.00 Matérn range: 8.67 Spatial SD: 2.22 Delta/hurdle model 2: ----------------------------------- Family: Gamma(link = 'log') coef.est coef.se (Intercept) 10.47 0.49 edu -0.09 0.01 hsp -0.04 0.01 blk 0.01 0.00 incmk 0.00 0.00 Dispersion parameter: 0.45 Matérn range: 13.16 Spatial SD: 2.54
ML criterion at convergence: 9654.486 See ?tidy.sdmTMB to extract these values as a data frame. **Possible issues detected! Check output of sanity().**

sanity(fit_dg) ✔ Non-linear minimizer suggests successful convergence ✔ Hessian matrix is positive definite ✔ No extreme or very small eigenvalues detected ✔ No gradients with respect to fixed effects are >= 0.001 ✔ No fixed-effect standard errors are NA ✔ No standard errors look unreasonably large ✔ No sigma parameters are < 0.01 ✔ No sigma parameters are > 100 ✖ A `range` parameter looks fairly large (> 1.5 the greatest distance in data) ℹ Try simplifying the model, adjusting the mesh, or adding priors ℹ Also make sure your spatial coordinates are not too big or small (e.g., work in UTM km instead of UTM m) Warning messages: 1: In min(x, na.rm = na.rm) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf 2: In max(x, na.rm = na.rm) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf 3: In min(x, na.rm = na.rm) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf 4: In max(x, na.rm = na.rm) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf 

 

I also attempted to estimate Spatial Error Models and Spatial Lag Models using lagsarlm() and errorsarlm() from the spatialreg package (I referred to this page: https://walker-data.com/census-r/spatial-analysis-with-us-census-data.html#spatial-subsets-and-spatial-predicates). However, when I drop zeros, more than half of the regions lose their neighbors, causing the code to fail.

4. Would modifying the spatial weights matrix allow lagsarlm() or errorsarlm() to work in this case? I generated the spatial weights matrix using this code, defining adjacency in a queen contiguity scheme:

wts <- df %>%
  poly2nb() %>%
  nb2listw()

I’d greatly appreciate any advice!


Best,
Joo
